title: Wrapper can dispatch a second live CLI session against one claim
description:
Filed by governor-1a5aca5d 12:56Z under the human's standing sweep directive, from THREE measured occurrences in one session (2026-08-16):

THE DEFECT. The agent wrapper can start a second CLI session for a workerId whose previous session is still alive and holding a claim. Both sessions then execute the same task concurrently in the shared worktree. The registry cannot see the duplicate — moe.list_workers shows ONE worker on the task because both sessions share the workerId; presence/staleness is per-workerId, not per-session.

OCCURRENCES, all disclosed in #general/#governors:
1. task-48c0c0db ~12:29Z: two live sessions under worker-5678886b; the earlier stood down mid-race (msg-ebbb27c0), the later committed. Resolved by luck + discipline: the earlier session happened to notice the other's drill cycling via file hashes.
2. task-6cbff010 ~12:55Z: same workerId, second session resumed at step-2 while the first had already LANDED the task into REVIEW (msg-7061495940) — the second session was working a stale plan state against moved bytes.
3. (Earlier class, 00:16: the wrapper re-dispatched task-b785 to a fresh worker while the prior worker's claim state was ambiguous — logged as wrapper-can-dispatch-an-already-claimed-task.)

BLAST RADIUS: duplicate mutation drills in the shared worktree, racing commits into one index, double complete_step calls, and QA grading a moving target. Only worker discipline (collision notes, stand-downs) prevented corruption each time.

LIKELY SEAM: the wrapper's crash-resume path ("CLI session ended N times... pausing auto-resume") plus its fresh-dispatch path can both fire after an outage window; nothing fences session generation. Fix directions the planner should weigh (measure first): a per-session nonce/generation in the registry so heartbeat/claims from a superseded session are refused with a stable code; wrapper-side single-flight lock per workerId; or daemon-side rejection of a second concurrent session registration for a live workerId.

Verification: a test that simulates two sessions under one workerId proves the second is refused (or fenced) with a stable reason code, and the first's claim/heartbeat continues unaffected.
definitionOfDone: The double-dispatch seam is identified by measurement (wrapper resume path and/or daemon registration) and the chosen fencing mechanism is implemented so a second concurrent session for a live workerId is refused or superseded with a stable reason code — never silently co-active.
The superseded/refused session's tool calls (heartbeat, complete_step, chat_send) fail closed with that code rather than mutating task state.
A test simulates the two-session race and pins the refusal code and layer; a mutation drill removing the fence turns it red.
The three occurrence records above are cited in the completion note as the reproduced-class evidence.
taskRails: Fail closed with stable reason codes; a fenced-out session must not be able to corrupt the claim, the worktree index, or the step ledger.
Do not break single-session resume-after-crash — the fence distinguishes a NEW session superseding a dead one (allowed, current behavior) from a second session co-existing with a LIVE one (refused).
Re-measure the wrapper dispatch/resume code paths on current bytes before planning; the occurrence timeline above is evidence, not a code map.

implementationPlan.description: SCOPE AND SEAM, by measurement, before any edit. Read-only step. The occurrence list in the description is from the OLD Moe harness (its tool names are moe.list_workers / heartbeat / complete_step). Epic rail 2 pins all development to D:/projexts/moe-next, so this task fixes the SAME DEFECT CLASS in moe-next's own wrapper and claim surfaces, and the completion note must say plainly that the old-Moe harness instance is out of scope under that rail. Re-confirm the architect's measurement at committed HEAD with `git grep`, do not trust this text: (a) moe-next ALREADY fences most of the class -- `work.claim` refuses a held item with the stable code `WORK_CLAIM_HELD` at layer `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` (apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.ts:160) and a non-claimant with `WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT` (:176), the frozen list being work/work-claim-contracts.ts:47-53; session generations already exist and a superseded generation refuses (apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority.ts:206 at layer BINDING, :355 SESSION_REPLAYED at layer GENERATION). (b) The wrapper serialises passes (`runOnce`, agent-wrapper.ts:355-365), skips items whose durable surface shows `step.claim !== null`, and holds an `active` Map keyed by workItemId (:343). THE HOLE: that `active` Map is IN-PROCESS ONLY, and the durable claim carries `expiresAt = clock() + claimTtlMs` (30 minutes, set in agent-wrapper-main.ts). When a claim EXPIRES while its agent child is still alive -- or when the wrapper process restarts with an empty `active` Map -- the surface reports the item unclaimed again and a SECOND live agent is staffed on it. The first child is never told; it keeps writing files in the shared worktree and only learns of the loss when a later command returns WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT. Write the confirmed seam into the step note naming exact files and lines. If measurement shows the hole is already closed, STOP and report that rather than adding a second fence.

QA's DoD 1 finding CONFIRMED exactly. `grep -n "staffingFence\|createAgentSessionFence" apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts` returns ZERO. The only production consumers are agent-wrapper.ts:90 (the optional config field) and :114 (`createStaffingGate(config.staffingFence)`). Since wrapper-main never passes one, `createStaffingGate(undefined).admit` returns null and always admits. The fence is inert in the shipped binary. QA is right and I am not disputing any part of the rejection.

THE BLOCKING DESIGN ITEM, RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT — this is the load-bearing result of this step, and it overturns the cheap fix.

QA required a staffing horizon or liveness probe landed WITH the injection, because a SIGKILL leaves the ADMITTED record unretired and wedges the item forever. A record TTL is explicitly disallowed (it reintroduces the very expiry defect the fence closes). So the probe must answer "is the recorded child actually alive?"

The obvious cheap implementation is to record the WRAPPER's own `process.pid` and, on a later admit, treat "recording wrapper is dead" as "record is stale, admit". It needs no contract change. **It is unsound, and the measurement says so:**

  apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:234-238
    // detached:true makes the shell the group leader. An accepted
    // negative-pid SIGKILL reaches it and every ordinary descendant.
    killProcessGroup(-child.pid, "SIGKILL");

The child is spawned `detached: true` as a process-group leader, and it is killed only by the wrapper explicitly running `killProcessGroup`. If the WRAPPER is SIGKILLed that line never runs, so the child SURVIVES as an orphan. "Recording wrapper is dead" therefore does NOT imply "child is dead" — and that is exactly the scenario the fence exists to catch. A wrapper-pid proxy would admit a second agent alongside a live orphaned child: the original defect, now with a fence that looks present.

So the probe MUST target the CHILD's pid. And the child pid is not reachable today:

  apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:75-81
    export type AgentSpawnStartResult =
      | { ok: false; code: SpawnInvocationRefusalCode; layer: ... }
      | { readonly ok: true; readonly exit: Promise<void> };

The accepted arm carries only `exit`. The spawner holds `child.pid` internally (agent-spawner.ts:188, 203, 238, 272) but never surfaces it.

SCOPE GROWTH, declared rather than taken silently. Implementing the liveness probe requires two files outside this plan's declared affectedFiles:
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts — widen the ok:true arm to carry the child pid
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts — populate it from the existing `child.pid`
Both are minimal and additive. I am flagging this rather than editing, because the plan predates the QA reject and never anticipated the probe.

DESIGN, ready to implement, fail-closed in every arm:
- `AgentLiveChildRecord` gains the child `pid`; the ADMITTED payload carries it.
- `foldLiveChild` currently inspects only event TYPES (agent-session-fence.ts:119-127) and never parses payloads — it must return the live record's pid so admit can probe it.
- `AgentSessionFenceConfig` gains an injected `isProcessAlive(pid): boolean` port, so tests never depend on real process ids.
- admit, on fold LIVE: alive -> refuse AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE; dead -> the record is stale, ADMIT; payload missing/unparseable pid -> refuse AGENT_STAFFING_RECORD_UNREADABLE (a new distinct code may be warranted for "stale record reclaimed" so it does not collapse into ordinary contention).
- PID REUSE fails SAFE: a recycled pid reads as alive, producing an over-eager refusal, which this module's own doc already calls recoverable (:22-26) because the retire path frees the item.

implementationPlan.description: RED on the fence contract, in a new apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.test.ts over a REAL SqliteEventStore opened on a temp file. The fence answers one question: may this wrapper staff this work item right now? Failing tests first: (1) item with no durable claim and no recorded live child -> ADMIT; (2) item with an ACTIVE unexpired claim -> refuse with the exact stable code and layer (assert both literals, never `ok === false`); (3) item whose claim has EXPIRED but whose durable live-child record has not been retired -> refuse with a DISTINCT stable code -- this is the reported class and it must not collapse into the held-claim code, or a later guard change makes the test vacuous; (4) item whose claim expired AND whose child was durably recorded as terminated -> ADMIT, because a genuinely dead predecessor must still be replaceable (task rail 2: single-session resume-after-crash must keep working); (5) a second fence query for the same item while the first admission is unretired, asked through a REOPENED store handle -> still refuses with the case-3 code, proving the record is durable rather than in-process. Every refusal asserts code AND layer, and every refusal case asserts the store's raw event count did not change.
implementationPlan.note:
RED on the liveness probe, the QA-blocking design item. Step re-scoped from the original text: the fence CONTRACT this step first specified is already built and committed at 54ad5e8, so re-writing it would be theatre. What is missing is the branch QA blocked on — a SIGKILLed wrapper leaves the ADMITTED record unretired and the item unstaffable FOREVER, strictly worse than the 30-minute exposure it replaces.

Design taken verbatim from worker-a83aecdf's step-1 handoff, including its trap: the probe MUST target the CHILD pid. Probing the recording WRAPPER's pid is the cheap fix and is UNSOUND — agent-spawner.ts:234-238 spawns `detached: true` and kills only via an explicit `killProcessGroup`, so a SIGKILLed wrapper leaves the child ALIVE as an orphan; "wrapper dead" would then admit a second agent beside a live child, i.e. the original defect wearing a fence.

Six cases added to agent-session-fence.test.ts, each asserting the exact code AND layer per global rail 1, and each refusal re-asserting `readEventHorizon()` is unmoved:
1. probes the CHILD pid, not the wrapper's — asserts the probed array is exactly [CHILD_PID] and `not.toContain(process.pid)`. This is the case that forbids the unsound substitution; without it a wrapper-pid probe passes every other case here.
2. CHILD_LIVE while the recorded pid is alive.
3. ADMITS once the recorded pid is dead — the anti-deadlock branch. A record TTL is explicitly NOT used: QA ruled it out because a TTL equal to the claim TTL reintroduces the expiry defect the fence closes.
4. LIVENESS_UNKNOWN when the probe THROWS — a new 4th refusal code, appended never reordered. "Cannot tell" must not collapse into either CHILD_LIVE or RECORD_UNREADABLE, and must never read as "dead".
5. RECORD_UNREADABLE when an ADMITTED payload carries no usable pid — driven by a real committed event, not a stub. foldLiveChild currently reads event TYPES only and never parses a payload, so this is the branch that must not fall through to "no pid, admit".
6. never probes when the claim is HELD — pins ordering, so a "dead child" answer can never override live contention.

Liveness is an INJECTED `isProcessAlive(pid)` port, so no case depends on the host's pid space. The helper defaults to `() => true` deliberately: defaulting to "dead" would make every stale case admit by accident.

PRODUCTION CHANGES
- agent-session-fence.ts: 4th refusal code AGENT_STAFFING_LIVENESS_UNKNOWN, APPENDED never reordered. AgentLiveChildRecord gains `childPid: number | undefined`; AgentSessionFenceConfig gains the injected `isProcessAlive(pid)` port. foldLiveChild now parses the ADMITTED payload (it previously read event TYPES only) and carries the live pid out. admit gained arm 3: alive -> CHILD_LIVE, dead -> ADMIT (stale record reclaimed), probe throws -> LIVENESS_UNKNOWN.
- childPidOf requires an INTEGER > 0. 0 and negatives address process GROUPS, not processes, so a negative pid would probe the wrong thing entirely; NaN/fractional can identify nothing.
- recordLiveChild omits the `childPid` KEY when there is no pid rather than persisting `undefined`/0/-1. A stored sentinel would look probeable while being unusable; an absent key routes to the UNREADABLE arm, which refuses.
- agent-spawn-contract.ts + agent-spawner.ts (the declared scope growth): the accepted arm now carries `pid: number | undefined`, captured from `child.pid` immediately after spawn and surfaced through SpawnAttempt. This is the CHILD's pid; the wrapper's own would be unsound for the reason recorded in step 2.
- agent-wrapper.ts passes `childPid: start.pid` at the existing record site. No new call site.

TWO DEFECTS MY OWN TESTS CAUGHT, both in code I had just written:

1. UNREADABLE POISONED THE AGGREGATE FOREVER. First version returned UNREADABLE from inside the fold loop the moment a pid failed to parse. A later RETIRED could then never be reached, so one pid-less admission wedged the item permanently — precisely the deadlock QA blocked this task on, reintroduced by the fix for it. Now the fold tracks `live = {childPid: number|null}` and decides only AFTER the last event, so RETIRED still clears an unprobeable record. The case "still retires a pid-less admission" is the regression guard and it FAILED before this change (measured, not assumed).

2. A DEFAULT PARAMETER SWALLOWED THE `undefined` UNDER TEST. `recordChild(store, 1, undefined)` re-triggered the helper's `= CHILD_PID` default, so the pid-less case recorded a REAL pid and passed for the wrong reason — a false green in the exact test written to prove fail-closed. Fixed by calling `recordLiveChild` directly there and narrowing the helper's parameter back to `number`, so `undefined` cannot be routed through it again.

FAIL-CLOSED LEDGER, every arm deliberate: unparseable pid -> refuse; absent pid -> refuse; probe throws -> refuse with a DISTINCT code, because "cannot tell" must never read as "dead"; pid reuse -> reads alive -> over-eager REFUSAL, which the module's doc already calls recoverable since retire frees the item. The only ADMIT added is a pid that probed dead.

implementationPlan.note:
The anti-deadlock proof at the WRAPPER level, which is the half QA blocked on. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator` -> `Test Files 9 passed (9)`, `Tests 112 passed (112)`, EXIT 0.

Added "re-staffs after a SIGKILLED wrapper, because the orphaned child probes DEAD". It is the race case with exactly ONE variable changed — the restarted wrapper's `isProcessAlive` answers false — so the pair forms a controlled comparison: same board, same solo port, same spawn stub, same release of the durable claim, same reopened store on a restarted wrapper. Live probe -> refuse AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE and spawnCalls stays [target]. Dead probe -> SPAWNED and spawnCalls becomes [target, target]. If those two ever agree, the probe has stopped being consulted, and the pair says so.

The SIGKILL state is produced durably rather than described: the claim is released through the real `writeClaim` path while the ADMITTED record is deliberately left in place, which is exactly what a killed wrapper leaves behind — no exit handler ran, so nothing retired it. The item reads UNCLAIMED to every reader (`activeClaim` nulls a released and an expired claim identically), so neither the surface nor the claim gate can be what answers; only the live-child record can.

I assert the spawn COUNT here as well as the outcome, for the mirror of the reason the race case does: two spawns is the CORRECT answer in this case, and an outcome-only assertion could not tell re-staffing apart from a report that never spawned at all.

STEP SCOPE, stated plainly rather than quietly narrowed. This step's text also asks for the DoD 2 "superseded side" — the first session's `work.renew` refusing with WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE. QA's rejection is explicit that mapping an existing work-claim refusal onto DoD 2 does not cover the reported class, because occurrence 2 was a LIVE, CALLING session; a refusal from the work-claim layer is a DIFFERENT layer answering, and presenting it as the staffing layer failing closed would be exactly the substitution global rail 1 forbids. worker-a83aecdf reached the same conclusion in the prior handoff and also declined to self-amend. implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, one per distinct claim, because "the fence exists" and "the fence fails closed" are different assertions. Drill 1 (the durable gate is load-bearing): delete the fence consultation from `staff`, leaving the in-process `active.has` check intact; the step-5 race test must go RED on its spawn-call-count assertion. If it stays green, the test is proving the in-process map rather than the durable fence -- reopen the fence's store between passes and re-run. Drill 2 (unreadable admits nothing): make the fence's unreadable-record branch return ADMIT instead of refusing; a named step-2 test must go RED. Drill 3 (the retire path is real): remove the retire call from the REJECTION branch of the `exit` handler; the case-4 dead-predecessor test must go RED, proving a crashed child does not permanently wedge the item. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME, and the exact assertion that failed -- a drill that reddens by crashing, or on a different assertion, has not proven the binding. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in this shared worktree), and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted per drilled file. One drill at a time: a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

QA re-review of retry 4cf3c35 (qa-12cda609). Recording durably because the remaining item needs an ARCHITECT decision, not worker code.

TWO OF THREE FAILED DoD ITEMS ARE FIXED AND DRILL-VERIFIED.

DoD 1 — fixed. createAgentSessionFence is now constructed in production at agent-wrapper-main.ts:244, with the store opened before the wrapper. Verified by drill, not by reading: deleting the `staffingFence:` property from that call reddens TWO tests in the new agent-wrapper-main.test.ts ("passes a staffingFence in...", "builds that fence from th..."). The wiring is now guarded against regression, which is what the original rejection asked for.

The hard-kill wedge I flagged as a blocking dependency is closed properly. The probe is on the CHILD pid, not the wrapper's, with the right reasoning: agent-spawner starts the child detached, so a SIGKILLed wrapper leaves a live orphan and "wrapper dead" would admit a second agent beside it. Drills confirm the subtle semantics are pinned: EPERM read as DEAD reddens ("reads a foreign-owned pid"), ESRCH read as ALIVE reddens ("reads a live pid as alive"). New AGENT_STAFFING_LIVENESS_UNKNOWN fails closed — making the probe-throw path ADMIT reddens. Pid-less admission reads UNREADABLE and refuses, while a later RETIRED can still clear it, so it fails closed WITHOUT reintroducing the wedge.

DoD 4 — fixed. task-48c0c0db, task-6cbff010 and task-b785 are now cited in the completion notes.

Gates re-run by me on a clean tree at 4cf3c35: daemon typecheck exit 0; full daemon suite UNEXCLUDED 107 files / 2192 tests exit 0.

Drill sweep: 7 mutants, 6 killed. One survivor, NON-BLOCKING and reported so it is not rediscovered: childPidOf's `Number.isInteger(pid) && pid > 0` clause has no test — accepting 0/negative/fractional pids leaves the suite green. Its failure direction is fail-closed (a 0 pid would probe the process GROUP, read alive, and refuse), so it wedges rather than admits, and no DoD item enumerates pid validation.

DoD 2 REMAINS UNMET AND IS NOT THE WORKER'S TO CLOSE. No tool-surface path fails closed with an AGENT_STAFFING_* code. The worker declined to self-amend and escalated; two workers have now done so. I agree with the escalation, and I want the reason stated precisely because it is a scope question, not an effort question:

DoD 2 names heartbeat, complete_step and chat_send. Those are MOE BOARD tools on the Moe MCP surface. What this task measured and fenced is the DAEMON's own agent wrapper, which staffs WORK ITEMS and whose agents call work_* tools. Those are two different systems. As written, DoD 2 may be asking this task to fence a surface it does not own and never touched — which is why every attempt to satisfy it maps onto a different layer (e.g. work.renew -> WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT), and a different layer answering is not this fence failing closed.

ARCHITECT DECISION NEEDED, one of:
(a) Amend DoD 2 to the daemon surface this task owns, or drop it as satisfied-by-design (a session refused pre-spawn never starts, so it makes no tool calls) — noting occurrence 2 was a session already live and calling, so that argument must be made explicitly rather than assumed; or
(b) Keep DoD 2 as written and file the Moe-board-surface fence as its own task, since it is a different codebase surface from this one.

I am holding this in REVIEW pending that decision rather than rejecting, because a third reject would send the worker back for code that is not the missing piece.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected: (a) fixing the old-Moe harness where the occurrences were observed -- epic rail 2 pins all development to D:/projexts/moe-next, so the deliverable is the same defect class closed in moe-next's own wrapper; the completion note must disclose that rather than let the title imply the harness was fixed. (b) A wrapper-side in-process lock -- one already exists (`active` Map plus serialised `runOnce`) and it is precisely what fails when the wrapper restarts or a second wrapper runs; more in-process state closes nothing. (c) Shortening claimTtlMs -- that shrinks the window but makes an expired-claim-over-a-live-child more frequent, not less. (d) Refusing all staffing on an expired claim -- breaks task rail 2, which requires resume-after-crash to keep working; the distinction the fence must draw is dead predecessor (admit) versus live predecessor whose claim merely expired (refuse). (e) Reusing WORK_CLAIM_HELD for the expired-but-live case, or adding the new codes to WORK_CLAIM_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES -- collapsing causes makes the new test one guard away from vacuous, and putting a wrapper-side staffing decision in the command surface's frozen list would misname which layer refused. Chose a small durable admission record consulted by the wrapper before session.open and work.claim, retired on every child-exit route, with a distinct stable code per cause and its own exported frozen code list.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at committed HEAD a42ae2f with `git grep <sym> HEAD`; the working tree is foreign-dirty and must not be trusted. Most of this fence already exists and must be COMPOSED, not rebuilt. DURABLE CLAIM: apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.ts:160 refuses `WORK_CLAIM_HELD` and :176 refuses `WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT`, both at layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; the frozen list is work/work-claim-contracts.ts:47-53; the kinds are work.claim/work.release/work.renew (:18-22). SESSION GENERATIONS: apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority.ts mints generation 1 (:164, :168), rotates to generation+1 on renew (:341), refuses a mismatched held generation at :206 (layer BINDING) and refuses a replayed rotation at :355 with SESSION_REPLAYED (layer GENERATION) -- supersession semantics exist, so this task consumes them rather than adding a parallel notion. WRAPPER: createAgentWrapper at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:141; `staff` mints a FRESH sessionId per spawn (`sess-wrap-${mintSecret()}`, :206), opens the session under the operator credential (:231), then has the AGENT claim under its own credential so the durable fence names the agent (:248); passes are serialised by `runOnce` (:355-365); staffing skips `step.claim !== null` and `active.has(workItemId)` (:339-343); the child's `exit` handler retires `active` and runs cleanupAuthority on BOTH fulfilment and rejection (:301-314), which is the natural retire hook. THE HOLE: `active` is a process-local Map and the claim carries a 30-minute expiresAt set in agent-wrapper-main.ts, so an expired claim over a still-live child, or a wrapper restart, re-opens staffing for an item that already has a running agent. NOTE for the worker: DoD 3's tool names (heartbeat, complete_step, chat_send) are old-Moe tools; the moe-next equivalents to test are work.renew, the work-progress command, and session credential authentication.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is a fence that is really the in-process map wearing a new name -- drill 1 exists to catch exactly that, and the race test must age the clock AND reopen the fence's backing store so the second pass cannot be refused by leftover memory. Second, a permanent wedge: if the retire path misses any exit route (throw, containment failure, process kill) an item becomes unstaffable forever, which is worse than the race it fixes and violates the task rail on resume-after-crash; drill 3 pins it. Third, two layers can refuse a superseded session (work-claim prerequisite and session-authority generation), so the DoD 3 tests must assert WHICH layer answered -- a second layer starting to answer first is the classic way these tests go quietly vacuous. Fourth, distinct causes need distinct codes; reusing WORK_CLAIM_HELD for the expired-but-live case would make case 3 indistinguishable from case 2. Fifth, close every SqliteEventStore handle on every path in tests -- a held handle kills the vitest worker outright. Sixth, mutation drills in this shared worktree must be restored by re-editing and verified with `git diff --numstat`; `git checkout` destroys peers' uncommitted work, and a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch so git reads clean. Finally, do not remove the existing in-process guard: it is still the correct cheap check inside one process, and the plan adds a gate rather than replacing one.

priorHandoffs.pitfalls: THE TRAP THAT WOULD SHIP A FAKE FIX. The cheap liveness probe is to record the WRAPPER's own process.pid and, on a later admit, treat 'recording wrapper is dead' as 'record is stale, admit'. It needs no contract change and looks right. It is UNSOUND. agent-spawner.ts:234-238 spawns the child `detached: true` as a process-group leader and kills it only because the wrapper explicitly runs `killProcessGroup(-child.pid, "SIGKILL")`. SIGKILL the WRAPPER and that line never runs, so the child SURVIVES as an orphan. 'Wrapper dead' therefore does not imply 'child dead' — which is exactly the scenario the fence exists to catch — and the proxy would admit a second agent alongside a live orphan: the original defect wearing a fence. Only a drill aimed at that specific case would catch it. SO: the probe MUST target the CHILD's pid, and the child pid is NOT reachable today — agent-spawn-contract.ts:75-81 accepted arm is `{ ok: true; exit: Promise<void> }`, while the spawner holds child.pid internally at :188, :203, :238, :272 and never surfaces it. SCOPE GROWTH, declared not taken: two files outside the plan's affectedFiles are required — agent-spawn-contract.ts (widen the ok arm to carry the pid) and agent-spawner.ts (populate it). Both additive; the plan predates the QA reject and never anticipated the probe, so get it blessed or split. DESIGN, fail-closed in every arm: AgentLiveChildRecord gains the child pid and the ADMITTED payload carries it; foldLiveChild (agent-session-fence.ts:119-127) currently inspects only event TYPES and never parses payloads, so it must return the live record's pid; AgentSessionFenceConfig gains an injected isProcessAlive(pid) port so tests never touch real process ids; admit on fold LIVE — alive => refuse AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE, dead => record is stale so ADMIT, pid missing or unparseable => refuse AGENT_STAFFING_RECORD_UNREADABLE (consider a distinct code for 'stale record reclaimed' so it does not collapse into ordinary contention). PID REUSE FAILS SAFE: a recycled pid reads as alive, giving an over-eager refusal, which the module's own doc at :22-26 already calls recoverable because the retire path frees the item. A RECORD TTL IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE SUBSTITUTE — QA ruled it out explicitly because a TTL equal to the claim TTL reintroduces the expiry defect the fence exists to close. Finally: do NOT wire the fence into agent-wrapper-main.ts without the probe landing in the same change; that is the permanent-deadlock outcome QA blocked on.
